technical_and_design_decisions: Implement acceptance tests as black-box tests through each module's supported public configuration and runtime interfaces, without changing production behavior.
Reuse the repository's existing test framework, build conventions, fixtures, and CI mechanisms wherever available.
Use deterministic local test doubles, embedded services, or containerized dependencies for mail, IP, syslog, SFTP, HTTP, and other external integrations.
Cover the primary successful flow plus key configuration, validation, error-handling, and boundary cases appropriate to each module.
Keep tests isolated, repeatable, and safe for parallel CI execution by using temporary files, unique ports, isolated directories, and cleanup fixtures.
Integrate all new acceptance tests into the standard CI build and configure failures to produce actionable logs and artifacts.
assumptions: The source repository, module implementations, build files, and an existing unit or integration test framework are available.
The eight modules already build successfully and do not require production-code feature changes to make acceptance testing possible.
Existing project documentation and module behavior are sufficient to derive acceptance scenarios; no new business requirements are expected.
CI runners can execute local processes and, where needed, containerized or embedded test dependencies.
External systems will be simulated or run locally; provisioning shared third-party environments is out of scope.
One workday represents one developer day of focused effort, including coding, local execution, and basic debugging.
The estimate includes implementation and developer verification, but not a separate QA execution cycle or long-term maintenance.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the eight target modules, existing test conventions, build lifecycle, CI configuration, and module-specific dependencies; identify acceptance scenarios and implementation gaps.
Establish or extend shared test utilities, lifecycle management, temporary resources, dependency startup and shutdown, test data, logging, and local execution configuration for the acceptance suite.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for Mail, including representative message retrieval or processing, configuration validation, message content handling, error behavior, cleanup, and deterministic mail-service fixtures.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for reactor-ip, including normal event or packet handling, relevant configuration options, malformed or unsupported input behavior, and repeatable network test fixtures.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for reactor-syslog, including syslog message ingestion, supported formats, configuration behavior, invalid input handling, and isolated UDP or TCP test setup.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for SFTP, including connection and authentication, remote file discovery or transfer, file-content handling, failure behavior, and an isolated SFTP server fixture.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for aggregator, including grouping or aggregation behavior, output correctness, configuration boundaries, empty or malformed input, and lifecycle or flush behavior.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for analytic-pmml, including loading a representative PMML model, successful scoring, input/output mapping, invalid model or data handling, and deterministic expected results.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for bridge, including input-to-output forwarding, routing or transformation configuration, lifecycle behavior, error handling, and assertions that no unintended records are lost or duplicated.

Implement and verify acceptance scenarios for http-client, including request construction, response handling, headers and payloads, status-code failures, timeout behavior, and a controllable local HTTP service.

Add all acceptance tests to the appropriate CI lifecycle, configure dependency and resource handling, execute repeated local and CI-equivalent runs, diagnose flaky behavior, and improve failure diagnostics.
Perform code and test review, clean up fixtures and configuration, document how to run and troubleshoot the acceptance suite, and complete a final full-build verification.
